rawToolsCapture.name: build_context
rawToolsCapture.title: Build Context
rawToolsCapture.description:
Build context from a memory:// URI to continue conversations naturally.

    Use this to follow up on previous discussions or explore related topics.

    Memory URL Format:
    - Use paths like "folder/note" or "memory://folder/note"
    - Pattern matching: "folder/*" matches all notes in folder
    - Valid characters: letters, numbers, hyphens, underscores, forward slashes
    - Avoid: double slashes (//), angle brackets (<>), quotes, pipes (|)
    - Examples: "specs/search", "projects/basic-memory", "notes/*"

    Timeframes support natural language like:
    - "2 days ago", "last week", "today", "3 months ago"
    - Or standard formats like "7d", "24h"

    Format options:
    - "json" (default): Structured JSON with internal fields excluded
    - "text": Compact markdown text for LLM consumption

url.description: memory:// URI pointing to discussion content (e.g. memory://specs/search)

project.description:
Project name to build context from. Optional - server will resolve using hierarchy.
    If unknown, use list_memory_projects() to discover available projects.

project_id.description:
Project external_id (UUID). Prefer this over `project` when known —
    it routes to the exact project regardless of name collisions across cloud
    workspaces. Takes precedence over `project`. Get from list_memory_projects().

depth.description: How many relation hops to traverse (1-3 recommended for performance)

timeframe.description: How far back to look. Supports natural language like "2 days ago", "last week"

page.description: Page number of results to return (default: 1)

page_size.description: Number of results to return per page (default: 10)

max_related.description: Maximum number of related results to return (default: 10)

output_format.description:
Response format - "json" for structured JSON dict,
"text" for compact markdown text

rawToolsCapture.name: recent_activity
rawToolsCapture.title: Recent Activity
rawToolsCapture.description:
Get recent activity for a project or across all projects.

    Timeframe supports natural language formats like:
    - "2 days ago"
    - "last week"
    - "yesterday"
    - "today"
    - "3 weeks ago"
    Or standard formats like "7d"

type.description:
Filter by content type(s). Can be a string or list of strings.
Valid options:
- "entity" or ["entity"] for knowledge entities
- "relation" or ["relation"] for connections between entities
- "observation" or ["observation"] for notes and observations
Multiple types can be combined: ["entity", "relation"]
Case-insensitive: "ENTITY" and "entity" are treated the same.
Default is entity-only. Specify other types explicitly to include
observations and relations.

depth.description: How many relation hops to traverse (1-3 recommended)

timeframe.description:
Time window to search. Supports natural language:
- Relative: "2 days ago", "last week", "yesterday"
- Points in time: "2024-01-01", "January 1st"
- Standard format: "7d", "24h"

project.description:
Project name to query. Optional - server will resolve using the
    hierarchy above. If unknown, use list_memory_projects() to discover
    available projects.

project_id.description:
Project external_id (UUID). Prefer this over `project` when known —
    it routes to the exact project regardless of name collisions across cloud
    workspaces. Takes precedence over `project`. Get from list_memory_projects().

output_format.description:
"text" returns human-readable summary text. "json" returns
a flat list of recent items.

rawToolsCapture.name: search_notes
rawToolsCapture.title: Search Notes
rawToolsCapture.description: Search across all content in the knowledge base with advanced syntax support.

query.description:
Optional search query string (supports boolean operators, phrases, patterns).
  Omit or pass None for filter-only searches using metadata_filters, tags, or status.

project.description:
Project name to search in. Optional - server will resolve using hierarchy.
    If unknown, use list_memory_projects() to discover available projects.

project_id.description:
Project external_id (UUID). Prefer this over `project` when known —
    it routes to the exact project regardless of name collisions across cloud
    workspaces. Takes precedence over `project`. Get from list_memory_projects().

search_all_projects.description:
Optional opt-in to search every accessible project. Ignored when
    `project` or `project_id` is supplied.

page.description: The page number of results to return (default 1)

page_size.description: The number of results to return per page (default 10)

search_type.description:
Type of search to perform, one of:
        "text", "title", "permalink", "vector", "semantic", "hybrid".
        Default is dynamic: "hybrid" when semantic search is enabled, otherwise "text".

output_format.description:
"text" preserves existing structured search response behavior.
"json" returns a machine-readable dictionary payload.

note_types.description: Optional list of note types to search (e.g., ["note", "person"])

entity_types.description: Optional list of entity types to filter by (e.g., ["entity", "observation"])

categories.description:
Optional list of observation categories for exact matching (e.g.,
       ["requirement"]). Pair with entity_types=["observation"] to return only
       observations whose category matches exactly.

after_date.description: Optional date filter for recent content (e.g., "1 week", "2d", "2024-01-01")

tags.description:
Optional tag filter (frontmatter tags); shorthand for metadata_filters["tags"].
  Accepts a list (["a", "b"]) or a comma-separated string ("a,b"), matching the
  write_note tags convention and the tag: query shorthand.

status.description: Optional status filter (frontmatter status); shorthand for metadata_filters["status"]

min_similarity.description:
Optional float to override the global semantic_min_similarity threshold
           for this query. E.g., 0.0 to see all vector results, or 0.8 for high precision.
           Only applies to vector and hybrid search types.

rawToolsCapture.name: read_note
rawToolsCapture.title: Read Note
rawToolsCapture.description: Read a markdown note by title or permalink.

identifier.description:
The title or permalink of the note to read
       Can be a full memory:// URL, a permalink, a title, or search text

project.description:
Project name to read from. Optional - server will resolve using the
    hierarchy above. If unknown, use list_memory_projects() to discover
    available projects.

project_id.description:
Project external_id (UUID). Prefer this over `project` when known —
    it routes to the exact project regardless of name collisions across cloud
    workspaces. Takes precedence over `project`. Get from list_memory_projects().

page.description:
Page of fallback-search results to use when the identifier does not
resolve to a note directly (default: 1). A direct or exact-title match
always returns the full note content — page/page_size never chunk the
note itself, and the title-match lookup pages through fixed-size pages
of title results until an exact match is found or results are
exhausted, regardless of page or page_size.

page_size.description:
Number of fallback-search results per page (default: 10). When no
match is found, this caps how many related-note suggestions are listed.

output_format.description:
"text" returns markdown content or guidance text.
"json" returns a structured object with title/permalink/file_path/content/frontmatter.

include_frontmatter.description:
When output_format="json", whether content should include the
opening YAML frontmatter block.

rawToolsCapture.name: edit_note
rawToolsCapture.title: Edit Note
rawToolsCapture.description: Edit an existing markdown note using various operations like append, prepend, find_replace, replace_section, insert_before_section, or insert_after_section.

identifier.description:
The exact title, permalink, or memory:// URL of the note to edit.
       Must be an exact match - fuzzy matching is not supported for edit operations.
       Use search_notes() or read_note() first to find the correct identifier if uncertain.

operation.description:
The editing operation to perform:
      - "append": Add content to the end of the note (creates the note if it doesn't exist)
      - "prepend": Add content to the beginning of the note (creates the note if it doesn't exist)
      - "find_replace": Replace occurrences of find_text with content (note must exist)
      - "replace_section": Replace content under a specific markdown header (note must exist)
      - "insert_before_section": Insert content before a section heading without consuming it (note must exist)
      - "insert_after_section": Insert content after a section heading without consuming it (note must exist)

content.description: The content to add or use for replacement

project.description:
Project name to edit in. Optional - server will resolve using hierarchy.
    Use "workspace/project" to route to a project in a specific cloud workspace.
    If unknown, use list_memory_projects() to discover available projects.

workspace.description:
Workspace slug, name, or tenant_id. When provided with `project`,
    routes as `workspace/project`. Cannot be combined with `project_id`.

project_id.description:
Project external_id (UUID). Prefer this over `project` when known —
    it routes to the exact project regardless of name collisions across cloud
    workspaces. Takes precedence over `project`. Get from list_memory_projects().

section.description: For replace_section operation - the markdown header to replace content under (e.g., "## Notes", "### Implementation")

find_text.description: For find_replace operation - the text to find and replace

expected_replacements.description: For find_replace operation - the expected number of replacements (validation will fail if actual doesn't match)

output_format.description:
"text" returns the existing markdown summary. "json" returns
machine-readable edit metadata.

project_id.description:

rawToolsCapture.name: list_memory_projects
rawToolsCapture.title: List Memory Projects
rawToolsCapture.description:
List all available projects with their status.

Shows projects from both local and cloud sources when cloud credentials
are available, merging by permalink to give a unified view.

Each project entry includes an `external_id` (UUID). Pass that value as the
`project_id` parameter on other tools to address a specific project
unambiguously across cloud workspaces — useful when the same project name
exists in more than one workspace.

output_format.description:
"text" returns the existing human-readable project list.
"json" returns structured project metadata.

rawToolsCapture.name: create_memory_project
rawToolsCapture.title: Create Memory Project
rawToolsCapture.description:
Create a new Basic Memory project.

Creates a new project with the specified name and path. The project directory
will be created if it doesn't exist. Optionally sets the new project as default.

project_name.description: Name for the new project (must be unique)

project_path.description: File system path where the project will be stored

set_default.description: Whether to set this project as the default (optional, defaults to False)

workspace.description:
Optional cloud workspace selector to create the project in. Slug is
preferred for AI callers, but tenant_id and unique name are also accepted.
When omitted, the connection's default workspace is used. Discover values
via `list_workspaces`. A workspace selector implies cloud routing:
without cloud credentials the call fails fast instead of silently
creating a local project (#954).

output_format.description:
"text" returns the existing human-readable result text.
"json" returns structured project creation metadata.

rawToolsCapture.name: delete_project
rawToolsCapture.title: Delete Project
rawToolsCapture.description:
Delete a Basic Memory project.

Removes a project from the configuration and database. This does NOT delete
the actual files on disk - only removes the project from Basic Memory's
configuration and database records.

project_name.description: Name of the project to delete

workspace.description:
Optional cloud workspace selector to delete the project from.
Slug is preferred for AI callers, but tenant_id and unique name are
also accepted. When omitted, the connection's default workspace is
used. A workspace selector implies cloud routing: without cloud
credentials the call fails fast, matching create_memory_project
behavior (#954).
